solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Movie containing most unlikely material

indicators.note: the movie word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: PIC is short for picture, a film
the last candidate is the least likely to be chosen

explanation.surface: A film is said to be full of the most improbable stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' sits at the end looking like part of the film's contents; it is the definition, and plastic is a material.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: plastic is the man-made material moulded into bottles, toys and bank cards.

clue.text: Hot tap turns this way

indicators.note: turning something round makes it run backwards

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
used as it stands

explanation.surface: A plumbing note: the hot tap twists in this direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as instructions for turning a tap; in fact the whole of H plus TAP turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a path is a way in the literal sense, a track you walk along, and also a course of action.

clue.text: Moderate state argued on a regular basis

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: take letters at a regular step: every other one

parts.note: the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of ArGuEd

explanation.surface: A middle-of-the-road politician's state keeps arguing its case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate state' looks like one phrase for a mild country; the definition is just 'Moderate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means ordinary or middling, as moderate does.

clue.text: Former partner avoiding more sex is characteristic

indicators.note: keep away from, so leave those letters out

parts.note: an ex is a former partner; these are the letters removed
extra means more
IT is old slang for sex (or sex appeal)

explanation.surface: Steering clear of further sex is typical of one's ex.
explanation.walkthrough: EXTRA plus IT makes EXTRAIT; the ex is avoided by dropping its opening EX.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trait is a distinguishing feature of someone's character, a characteristic.

clue.text: Fanciful style captures timeless quality

indicators.note: the style word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: chic is stylishness

indicators.note: without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: merit is a good quality; losing its T leaves MERI

explanation.surface: A fanciful look manages to catch some enduring quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless quality' reads as praise, but 'timeless' is an instruction to drop T from MERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimeric means imaginary or fanciful, like a chimera.

clue.text: I'm surprised about backing a real outsider

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: an exclamation of surprise
on means about, as in a book on birds
a as in 'fifty pence a go' means per

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at people putting money on a rank outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' suggests betting on a horse, which suits the outsider; here it reverses OH ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone or something with no chance, a real outsider in a race.

clue.text: Nod head at introduction to empress

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
used as it stands

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of empress

explanation.surface: A courtier bows his head as the empress is presented.
explanation.walkthrough: An uncommon word, built plainly from its parts once 'head' is read as NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare technical word: nutate comes from Latin nutare, to nod, and describes a nodding motion of the head or a plant.

clue.text: Beehive possibly preserves constant location for feeding young

indicators.note: keeps something safe inside it

parts.note: a beehive is a tall, piled-up hairstyle: high hair
C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A beehive stores honey in one fixed place where its larvae are fed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all bees and brood, but the beehive is the hairdo and the young are babies.
explanation.definitionFit: A high chair is where a baby sits to be fed.

clue.text: Pressure someone enduring wall-to-wall coverage?

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
one who lasts

explanation.surface: Someone is under constant media pressure, with coverage everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wall-to-wall coverage' means saturation news; the question mark flags the literal reading, stuff spread over every wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster is what covers a wall from one side to the other.

clue.text: Trooper is last in company to turn 18

indicators.note: take the final letter of the next word
turning the letters over rearranges them

parts.note: used as they stand, for rearranging
last letter of company

explanation.surface: A young soldier turns eighteen, the last in his unit to come of age.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' looks like an age; it is a cross-reference to 18 down, ARCHIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an archive and a repository are both places where records or objects are stored for safekeeping.

clue.text: Head doctor's article is, in part, absurd

indicators.note: IS goes inside the other piece

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: made nonsense of, so rearranged

parts.note: PART rearranged; IS goes inside it
used as it stands

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist's paper is partly nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' looks like 'partly'; it is IS placed in a jumbled PART. 'Head doctor' is slang for a psychiatrist or therapist.
explanation.definitionFit: Head doctor is informal for a psychiatrist, like shrink, and a therapist treats troubles of the mind.

clue.text: See doctor to check skin condition having left hospital

indicators.note: to hold in check: the doctor holds the next piece inside

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

indicators.note: having left means having gone away, so the hospital's letter departs from the word

parts.note: a rash; losing H leaves RAS
H is the map abbreviation for hospital; these are the letters removed

explanation.surface: A patient visits the GP to have a skin complaint looked at after discharge from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See doctor' reads as one medical instruction; 'See' alone is the definition, as in 'I see what you mean'.
explanation.definitionFit: See in its sense of understand, as in 'I see what you mean', which is what grasp means too.

clue.text: Gives legal validity to condition in each statute

indicators.note: to condition something is to work it into a new shape

parts.note: used as they stand, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A law is made valid by a condition written into every statute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condition' reads as a noun, a clause in a law; it is a verb telling you to rework the letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To authenticate a document is to confirm it as genuine and legally valid.

clue.text: Relationships restricting development of fiery young men

indicators.note: the first word hems the next piece in
the letters develop into a new order

parts.note: bonds are ties between people
FIERY rearranged

explanation.surface: Relationships hold back hot-headed lads from growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiery young men' reads as one phrase; 'fiery' is the fodder and 'young men' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: boyfriends are typically young men, the male partners in romantic relationships.

clue.text: Prove sacked assistant spent more than necessary

indicators.note: ransacked, turned upside down, so rearranged

parts.note: PROVE rearranged
an aid is a helper

explanation.surface: Show that the fired assistant had been paid too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' belongs with 'assistant' in the surface, a dismissed employee; it is actually rearranging PROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense matches past tense: having overpaid, you handed over more money than the bill required.

clue.text: Iron and gold boxes belonging to academic

indicators.note: puts in a box, holding the next piece inside

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
as in 'the house of my father'
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An iron-and-gold strongbox that is the property of a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron and gold' looks like the chemical symbols FE and AU; iron is the verb, to press clothes, and heraldic gold is OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a professor holds the top teaching rank at a university, so is an academic.

clue.text: Repeat what causes standards to deteriorate?

parts.note: par is the standard level
to rot is to decay

explanation.surface: Asking whether repetition is what makes standards slip.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'par rot', standards deteriorating; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words without thought, as a parrot mimics speech, so it means repeat.

clue.text: Noble argument against valuable item being returned

parts.note: as in pros and cons

indicators.note: sent back, so its letters run in reverse

parts.note: an asset is something of value; reversed to TESSA

explanation.surface: An aristocrat objects to handing back a treasured possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' could be an adjective; it is the noun, a titled person.
explanation.definitionFit: Contessa is the Italian title of a countess, a woman of noble rank, so the noun noble fits.

clue.text: Continue to signal large vessel

parts.note: to flag is to signal
as in 'go on'

explanation.surface: A ship keeps signalling to a big vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large vessel' suggests a ship at sea; it is a big jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a big bottle or jug with a handle, holding wine or ale, and a vessel is any container for liquid.

clue.text: Author's supporting chief source of historical information

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means sitting underneath

parts.note: arch means chief, as in arch-enemy
the author (the setter, I) has: I'VE

explanation.surface: A writer is backing the main source of historical facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author's' reads as possessive, but in crosswords the author is the setter, I, and the apostrophe S stands for has.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive holds original documents and records, which historians consult as primary sources.

clue.text: Sad individual is more sensitive about argument

indicators.note: goes around the next piece

parts.note: sorer means more tender
a row is a quarrel (rhymes with cow)

explanation.surface: A sad soul is extra touchy about a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Row here rhymes with cow: a noisy quarrel. The container splits the comparative after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorrower is someone who grieves.

clue.text: Irregular method to attract backing

parts.note: a way of doing something

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: to draw a crowd is to attract it; reversed to WARD

explanation.surface: An unorthodox approach to winning support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as support, the thing sought; it reverses DRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayward means unpredictable and not following a set pattern, hence irregular.

clue.text: Youthful nurse put forward a proposal
Half of brilliant people agree little by little

indicators.note: keep only the first half of the word

parts.note: INCREDIBLE, brilliant, cut to its first five letters
men as in people generally
figures that tally agree

explanation.surface: Half the bright sparks slowly come round to agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant' must first become INCREDIBLE before it can be halved.
explanation.definitionFit: Incrementally means by small steps, little by little.

clue.text: Cross and belligerent to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the word is used

parts.note: inside belLIGERent

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed and somewhat combative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, a synonym for belligerent; it is the noun, a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A liger is a cross between a lion and a tigress.

clue.text: Present judge to auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this is how it sounds

parts.note: a judge hears a case

explanation.surface: Showing a judge's findings to an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant checking books; here it is one who listens.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means present, as when answering a roll call.

clue.text: Secures protection for digital assets?

definitions.meaning: to nail something down is to fix it
fingernails shield the tips of the digits

explanation.surface: A company locks down safeguards for its online holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital assets' sounds like cryptocurrency or files; the question mark flags the other sense, fingers and toes (digits).
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fix it firmly, and nails protect the tips of fingers.

clue.text: Model had style

parts.note: a design is a model or pattern
to have a meal is to eat it: had = ate

explanation.surface: A fashion model was stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' reads as a noun about fashion; it is the verb, to name or title.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to call them by a title, and to designate is likewise to name or officially call.

clue.text: He takes coats from people attending in rotation

indicators.note: rotating the word carries its last letter round to the front

parts.note: people attending to a speaker are hearers

explanation.surface: A cloakroom attendant takes guests' coats in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The coats are fleeces: the final S of HEARERS rotates to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearer clips the fleece off sheep; the fleece is the animal's woolly coat, taken from it.

clue.text: Diminish what's left of attention span

indicators.note: the leftmost part of a word, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of attention
to span a river is to bridge it

explanation.surface: Complaining that attention spans are shrinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's left of' sounds like a remnant; in an across word, the left end is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book is to cut it down, so it diminishes in length.
